topic: Cut-aware temporal history and allocation conformance
topic_zh: 切镜感知的时序历史与缓冲分配一致性
scope: Authored-cut toy grayscale EMA, raster conformance and Node CPU allocation. No inferred cut detector, neural video, motion reprojection, photographic quality or GPU timing.

checks.name: buffer-equivalence-16
checks.detail: 16×12 rasters give exact same output with reused and allocated history buffers

checks.name: buffer-equivalence-48
checks.detail: 48×32 rasters give exact same output with reused and allocated history buffers

checks.name: buffer-equivalence-96
checks.detail: 96×64 rasters give exact same output with reused and allocated history buffers

checks.name: authored-cut-reset
checks.detail: authored cut resets the actual displayed history to the current noisy raster

checks.name: persistent-ghosts
checks.detail: 306 stale-object pixels above 0.35 persist without reset; gated count is 0

checks.name: same-shot-history
checks.detail: within the uncut first shot both history policies are identical

checks.name: exact-revisit
checks.detail: reverse frame visitation reproduces exact history output

checks.name: invalid-contract
checks.detail: invalid authored cut is rejected with valid history contract retained

checks.name: actual-screen-match
checks.detail: actual current and reset-screen PNGs are identical at the cut

checks.name: mobile-layout
checks.detail: 390px temporal-history controls fit without horizontal overflow

checks.name: reduced-motion
checks.detail: reduced motion starts still and manual frame seeking remains available

timing_note: Median of 7 alternating warmed Node CPU runs for 120-frame reconstruction. Both timing paths reset on the same cut and have exact outputs. Source rasters still allocate. Persistent-history quality baseline is a separate comparison.

protocol.function: authored shot key → history validity → reset or accumulate → synthetic raster → projected console screens

robustness.name: Moving the authored cut retains ghost-free reset
